verses.1: On the twenty-fourth day of this month, the Israelites gathered with fasting and wearing sackcloth with dust on them.
verses.2: The Israelites separated themselves from all foreign people, stood, and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their ancestors.
verses.3: They stood in their place and read from the Book of the Teaching of their God, confessing and bowing toward the LORD their God.
verses.4: Then Joshua, the son of Kadmiel, and Bani, the son of Sarabiah, and the Levites who stood on the platform cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
verses.5: The Levites—Joshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Pethahiah—said, "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from eternity to eternity. May he bless the name of his glorious majesty, and may he be exalted over all praise and glory."
verses.6: Ezra said, "You are the one, O LORD, alone. You made the heavens—the heavens of the heavens and all their hosts, the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You give life to all of them. And the hosts of heaven bow to you."
verses.7: You are the God who chose Abram and brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.
verses.8: You found his heart faithful before you and made a covenant with him to give him the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites. You fulfilled your words, for you are just.
verses.9: You saw the distress of our ancestors in Egypt, and you heard their cry by the Red Sea.
verses.10: You performed signs and wonders in Egypt, in Pharaoh and all his servants, and in all the people of his land. For you knew that they had grown proud against you. You made a name for yourself, as it is to this day.
verses.11: You split the sea before them, and they crossed through the midst of the sea on dry land, while you cast their pursuers into the deep like a stone into the mighty waters.
verses.12: You led them by a pillar of cloud by day and by a pillar of fire by night to light the way they should take.
verses.13: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, giving them just judgments, true teachings, good decrees, and good commandments.
verses.14: You made your Sabbath known to them, and you gave commandments, decrees, and a Teaching through your servant Moses.
verses.15: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and water from the rock for their thirst, and you said to them, "Go in and possess the land I have stretched out my hand to give you."
verses.16: But they and our ancestors rebelled and hardened their necks and did not listen to your commandments.
verses.17: They refused to hear and did not remember the wonders you had performed among them. They hardened their necks and gave their heads to return to their slavery in Egypt. Yet you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and you did not abandon them.
verses.18: Even when they made for themselves a molten calf and said, "This is your God who brought you out of Egypt," and made great transgressions,
verses.19: you, in your great mercy, did not abandon them in the wilderness. You did not let the pillar of cloud depart from above them by day to lead them on the way, nor did the pillar of fire cease by night to light their path.
verses.20: You gave your good Spirit to teach them, and you did not withhold your manna from their mouths, nor did you deny them water for their thirst.
verses.21: You sustained them in the wilderness for forty years without lack. Their clothing did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
verses.22: You gave them kings and nations, and you divided them into portions, and they possessed the land of Sihon and the land of the king of Heshbon and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
verses.23: You multiplied their children like the stars of the heavens, and you brought them into the land you had promised to their ancestors to give them, and they possessed it.
verses.24: You crushed before them the people who lived in the land of the Canaanites, and you gave them into their hands, along with their kings and their peoples, to do with them as they pleased.
verses.25: They captured fortified cities, fertile land, houses full of every good thing, wells dug, vineyards and olive groves and trees yielding abundant food. They ate and were filled and grew fat and delighted in your great goodness.
verses.26: But they rebelled and turned away from you. They cast your Teaching behind them and killed your prophets who had testified to them in order to turn them back to you, and they committed great transgressions.
verses.27: So you gave them into the hand of their oppressors, who oppressed them. In their time of distress they cried out to you, and you heard from heaven. In your great mercy you gave them saviors who rescued them from the hand of their oppressors.
verses.28: But when they were at rest, they again did evil in your sight. You abandoned them into the hands of their enemies, and they oppressed them, and they again cried out to you. You heard from heaven and in your great mercy rescued them many times.
verses.29: You testified to them to turn them back to your Teaching. But they did not listen, and in your decrees and judgments they sinned, which if a person had done, he would have lived. They gave a rebellious shoulder and hardened their necks, and they did not listen.
verses.30: You sustained them for many years and testified to them by your Spirit through your prophets. Yet they did not listen, so you gave them into the hands of the peoples of the land.
verses.31: But in your great mercy you did not bring an end to them, nor did you abandon them, for you are a God of mercy and compassion.
verses.32: And now, our God, the great, mighty, and awesome God who keeps covenant and steadfast love, do not let all the affliction we have encountered—our kings, our officials, our priests, and our prophets, and our ancestors, and all your people from the days of the kings of Assyria until today—be small in your sight.
verses.33: You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for you have dealt faithfully, and we have acted wickedly.
verses.34: Our kings, our officials, our priests, and our ancestors did not keep your Teaching, nor did they listen to your commandments or to the testimonies you gave them.
verses.35: Even in your kingdom and in the great good you gave them, and in the wide and fertile land you gave before them, they did not serve you, nor did they turn from their evil deeds.
verses.36: Now we are servants, and the land you gave to our ancestors to eat its fruit and enjoy its goodness—now we are servants on it.
verses.37: Its produce goes to the kings you have placed over us because of our sins. They rule over us and our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress.

notes:
Notes
- v. 20: "good Spirit" — refers to the Spirit of the LORD, rendered as "good" to emphasize its life-giving purpose.
- v. 23: "as the stars of the heavens" — consistent with Genesis 15:5, where the multiplication of Israel is compared to the stars.
- v. 33: "you have dealt faithfully" — "faithfully" as a translation of אֱמֶת (emeth) to emphasize truthfulness and fidelity in God's dealings.
- v. 36-37: The Septuagint adds more explicit reference to the kings and their rule, but the Hebrew is clear and direct. No adjustment to the Hebrew sense was necessary.
